activity: 1762 stars, 367 forks, 114 open issues, Apache-2.0, created 2025-12-29, last push 2026-07-23 (commit 9a1f4dd5 "Rename task metadata sections to sandbox (#1037)") — ~7 weeks stale as of 2026-09-11. 4079 files in the tree; 87 task dirs under tasks/; 276 SKILL.md files.
whatItIs: A real, runnable agent benchmark plus the review apparatus around it — not a rule collection. 87 containerised tasks (task.md prompt + Dockerfile + environment/skills/ + oracle/solve.sh + verifier/test_outputs.py), executed through the external `bench` CLI (benchflow SDK, separate repo) on Docker/Modal/Daytona. Its central question, stated verbatim in .agents/skills/task-review/references/audit-skillsbench.md:5, is "does shipping a skill change the answer?" — i.e. it measures instruction documents by the downstream task outcome of an agent that did or did not have them.
method: A task is a sealed experiment: the human-written prompt in tasks/<id>/task.md never names the skills (AGENTS.md:43), the answer is derived by computation in oracle/solve.sh (AGENTS.md:46), and grading is outcome-only pytest in verifier/test_outputs.py producing a 0..1 reward (AGENTS.md:45). The document under test is mounted at runtime, not baked in: `bench eval run --skill-mode with-skill --skills-dir …` versus `--skill-mode no-skill`. The review protocol in .agents/skills/task-review/scripts/run_experiments.sh runs five configs per task — oracle, then claude×{skills,no-skills}, codex×{skills,no-skills} — and hard-aborts at line 98 unless the oracle returns reward 1.0, so the answer key is validated before any agent run is trusted. scripts/parse_results.py folds the runs into a summary.json of reward, passed/failed test names and tokens. Then a two-layer trajectory audit reads trajectory/acp_trajectory.jsonl: the general layer (references/audit-general.md, 15 principles P1–P15 in three cost tiers, with a per-job JSON schema at :317 and an aggregation rule at :293) buckets every failure as hard / unfair_instruction / unfair_test / unfair_env / capability_gap / ignored_instruction (:90) and splits format loss from reasoning loss (:130); the SkillsBench layer (references/audit-skillsbench.md) adds SB-1 "was the document read at all" (VERIFIED/PARTIAL/NOT_INVOKED, detected per-harness from the tool-call log, :7–62), SB-2 the with/without reward delta in percentage points with outcomes helped/hurt/no-op and a required quoted unlock or misled line (:64–113), and SB-3c a purely mechanical check that the router file was read but its references/*.md never opened (:145–160). Aggregation at :190 maps the signals to authoring advice: NOT_INVOKED on every config → "skill never discovered — likely description / placement issue"; SB-3c on the strongest model → "make the workflow more directive". Separately, docs/instruction-guidelines.md prescribes six criteria for the prompt prose (imperative, absolute paths, structured requirements, success criteria, constraints, context first) and reports a conformance audit of 330 terminal-bench tasks.
measures: Yes, and by outcome rather than by opinion — this is the rare case. Three distinct rulers: (1) reward delta in pp between the with-document and without-document arms of the same model on the same sealed task (audit-skillsbench.md:64–113); (2) mechanical read-log facts about the document — read at all / read only the top level / read but workflow not followed (:7–62, :145–160); (3) a control-integrity scan, experiments/scripts/gcp_setup/run_opencode_gcp_docker_ablation.py:42–53 and :692–719, that greps the without-skills trajectories for skill-loader markers and fails the trial if the control arm was contaminated. But the measurements are apparatus, not results: every figure script under docs/paper-figures/ is labelled "This script is fully synthetic" (README.md "⚠️ Synthetic data"; 03_tsapr_attribution_domain.py:10), so the headline numbers quoted in that README (+14.4 pp curated skills, etc.) are drawn from `_synthetic_rates(seed=42)`, and docs/skills-research/RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.md's RQ1 table still reads TBD / TBD / TBD. The runnable ablation implements two arms only (CONDITIONS = ("with-skills", "without-skills"), :40); the four-condition design (Distractor → No Skills → Self-Generated → Curated) exists only in the synthetic figure script and in target tables. The leaderboard JSONs under integrations/agentbeats/leaderboard/results/ are smoke fixtures with a placeholder participant UUID.

transferable.approach: A no-document control arm, scored as a delta. Run the same reader questions with the docs removed and report right-answers-with-docs minus right-answers-without-docs, with three named outcomes: helped, hurt, no-op.
transferable.whereItLives: benchflow-ai/skillsbench .agents/skills/task-review/scripts/run_experiments.sh:103-106 (four run_one calls: claude×{yes,no}, codex×{yes,no}) and .agents/skills/task-review/references/audit-skillsbench.md:64-113 (the skill_impact JSON block, delta_pp, outcome)
transferable.whyItMightWork: terse's 3→6 result is a single with-docs arm. It cannot separate "the doc taught the reader" from "a fresh model guesses 3 of 6 from the repo name and the code anyway". A no-docs arm turns the audit score into an attributable effect of the document, which is the claim the plugin actually wants to make.
transferable.collidesWith: Doubles the seat count in audit (one fresh cheap model per question becomes two), which collides with the audit's cheapness and with the standing no-large-fan-outs rule. Also collides with terse's failure taxonomy: a question the no-docs arm already answers is neither lie nor placement nor findability — it is a question that measures nothing, a fourth class terse has no bucket for.

transferable.approach: Mechanical failure classification from the reader's read log instead of judgment. SB-1: no doc file was ever opened → "never discovered". SB-3c: `top_level_only = bool(skill_files) and not sub_files` — the router was read, the linked detail file never was.
transferable.whereItLives: benchflow-ai/skillsbench .agents/skills/task-review/references/audit-skillsbench.md:7-62 (detect_skill_invocations, statuses VERIFIED|PARTIAL|NOT_INVOKED) and :145-160 (SB-3c, three lines of Python)
transferable.whyItMightWork: terse's lie / placement / findability split is currently an auditor's opinion about why a reader got it wrong. Two of those three classes have an objective shadow in the reader's tool log: findability = the file was never opened; placement = the entry file was opened but the file holding the answer was not. Only "lie" then needs judgment. Converting two classes from opinion to evidence is exactly the measurement-first move terse is built on, and it costs nothing extra per run.
transferable.collidesWith: Requires the reader seat to browse a filesystem and emit a tool log. If terse's audit hands the reader a concatenated bundle of .md text rather than a directory, there is no read log and this cannot be lifted without changing how readers are given the docs — which would itself change what findability means.

transferable.approach: Gate the run on an oracle. Before any reader is scored, a run with full access must score 100%; if it does not, abort and fix the key rather than reporting a document failure.
transferable.whyItMightWork: terse already derives the answer key from the code, but nothing proves the key is reachable from the code by a reader of ordinary skill. An oracle pass separates "the doc failed to say it" from "the question has no answer in this repository" — the single most likely way an audit score lies. It is one extra seat per audit, not per question.
transferable.collidesWith: Nothing in terse contradicts it; it inserts a step before scoring rather than replacing one. It does add a hard stop that can block an audit on a bad question.

transferable.approach: A declared noise floor and trial count on every delta. "Single-trial deltas with |Δ| < 30 pp are likely noise. Always note the trial count alongside the verdict."
transferable.whereItLives: benchflow-ai/skillsbench .agents/skills/task-review/references/audit-skillsbench.md:114-117 (Trial-count caveat), and the in-line hedge at :87 — "n=1; needs ≥3 trials to call"
transferable.whyItMightWork: terse's headline is 3/6 → 6/6 on one repository at n=1 per question. Six binary items at one trial each is a very wide interval; by skillsbench's own rule a reviewer would refuse to call anything from a single run. Publishing the trial count and a floor next to the score costs one sentence and makes the number defensible instead of impressive.
transferable.collidesWith: Directly weakens the plugin's existing marketing claim ("moved six reader questions from 3 right to 6 right"), and re-running each question ≥3 times triples audit cost.

transferable.approach: Treat "the rewrite made it worse" as a first-class, evidence-bearing outcome: Δ ≤ −10 pp is `hurt` and requires a quoted `misled_quote` — the exact line of the document that misled the reader.
transferable.whyItMightWork: revise's four passes and bake-off assume the winner is an improvement, verified only in aggregate. A per-question regression table with a mandatory quoted culprit line catches the case where a rewrite fixes two questions and breaks one — the aggregate 3→6 hides it — and it names the sentence to revert rather than re-running the whole chain.
transferable.collidesWith: Sits inside revise's repair pass rather than replacing anything, but it contradicts the bake-off's judge-picks-a-winner framing: a writer can win on the measured failures and still regress a question that was already right.

weaknesses: Three real ones. First, the results are missing: docs/paper-figures/README.md states plainly that every script uses synthetic placeholder data, and RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.md's RQ1 ("do skills help?") table is still TBD/TBD/TBD as of its January 2026 date — so the repo ships a measurement apparatus whose central measurement it has not published in-tree. The only real conditions implemented are two (with/without); Distractor and Self-Generated exist as design targets and synthetic figure axes. Second, cost: the review protocol is five containerised agent runs per document, on Docker or a cloud microVM, with OAuth for two frontier models — three to four orders of magnitude more expensive per document than terse's cheap-reader sweep, and its own docs say single-trial deltas under 30 pp are noise, so the honest version is ≥15 runs. Third, its prescriptive layers are the exact pattern terse already rejected: docs/instruction-guidelines.md is a six-criteria writing standard with a conformance audit ("15% of tasks fail 3+ criteria", "TB2 imperative tone 34%") that produces compliance percentages and no rewrite; .github/scripts/lint_skill_frontmatter.py is a CI gate on doc metadata; policy-rubric.md:16 proposes running GPTZero on prose and flagging >70%. None of that should be lifted. Also note SkillsBench deliberately makes document quality non-blocking — audit-general.md:315 "skills_utilization (delta) is NOT a blocking criterion" — because it is primarily a model benchmark that happens to A/B documents; the document-quality read is a by-product, and docs/harnesses/skill-invocation-surfaces.md:2 shows why any such delta is harness-confounded (Codex injects the whole body as a user-role fragment with no trajectory event; Claude Code does description-in-context progressive disclosure).
